assertions.description: BackgroundFetchManager is the interface the feature governs.
backgroundFetch hangs off a ServiceWorkerRegistration, which is why the API needs a service worker at all.
responseReady is where a CORS failure surfaces: the record exists, and reading its response is what is refused.
Background Fetch is a secure-context API, which the demos depend on and which this page satisfies on localhost.

The reference behaviour Background Fetch is being aligned to: a cross-origin no-cors fetch yields an opaque response the page cannot read. http://127.0.0.1 and http://localhost are different origins on the same server, which makes this checkable locally.
The control for the assertion above: the same cross-origin URL WITH Access-Control-Allow-Origin is readable. If this failed, the previous assertion would prove nothing.

backgroundFetch.fetch() is gated on transient user activation, so calling it from script with no gesture must reject. This is why the cross-origin demo asks the reader to click each button rather than running both itself.
assertions.test: (async()=>{try{const reg=await navigator.serviceWorker.getRegistration('/v154/cors-enforcement-for-background-fetch/');if(!reg||!reg.backgroundFetch)return false;await reg.backgroundFetch.fetch('conf-activation-'+Math.floor(performance.now()),['/public/media/jpeg-xl/image.avif'],{title:'conformance probe',downloadTotal:17317});return false;}catch(e){return e instanceof TypeError;}})()
